_how_to_read: verdict is our corpus against the outside claim: confirmed, contradicted, not_confirmed (tested, nothing passes the rule), untestable. result = win rate of the version WITH the trait in same-account, order-balanced pairs of launch posts (50% = no effect), 95% interval from resampling accounts, likes ratio with/without inside accounts, adjusted ratio holding the other traits fixed. Outcome is likes relative to the account's own trailing median.

hypotheses.claim: A launch post should end with a call to action to use the product (try it, get started, sign up).
hypotheses.note: Lee, Hosanagar and Nair (R:K07/R:B01, 106k Facebook brand posts) point the other way for overtly persuasive content.

hypotheses.claim: Gating access behind a waitlist, invites or a research preview makes the launch post travel further (scarcity).
A waitlist launch does better than an available-now launch.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: Asking for a reply or repost in exchange for access ('comment X and I'll DM you', 'RT for an invite') lifts the post.
hypotheses.note: X's code labels engagement bait as spam (no out-of-network distribution) and X said in 2026 that Grok pushes solicitation down; no effectiveness data exists outside either.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: Explicitly asking readers to share or support ('please RT', 'would love your support') raises sharing.
hypotheses.note: Tan, Lee and Pang 2014: same author, same link, 11,404 pairs; 2014 Twitter.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: Saying the product is free lifts the launch post (zero-price effect).
hypotheses.note: The controlled evidence is on purchase choice in lab experiments, not on social posts.

hypotheses.claim: Open-source / open-weights releases travel further than closed launches.
hypotheses.note: R:B08 (controlled, 2,370 repositories) is about tweets raising GitHub stars, not about open-source posts getting more engagement.

hypotheses.claim: Offering credits, a discount, a launch deal or a prize lifts the launch post.
hypotheses.note: R:B01 (large observational, Facebook) found price and deal content LOWERS engagement; our result agrees with that study and contradicts the playbook.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: Stating the price lowers engagement with a brand post.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: Naming customers or users (social proof) lifts the launch post.
hypotheses.note: R:B07 is Kickstarter pitch wording (45k projects), not X.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: Naming investors or an accelerator (backed by, YC) lifts the launch post.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: A concrete number anywhere in the post (informativeness) makes it travel further.
hypotheses.note: Launch track: a number in the FIRST line passed at 55.8% (50.5 to 60.9), its weakest finding.

hypotheses.claim: Leading with a benchmark result (state of the art, x times faster, a leaderboard rank) makes an AI launch travel.
A benchmark chart image does better than another image.
hypotheses.note: Text proxy: a benchmark claim in a post with an image. What the image shows is not read here (media track).

hypotheses.claim: Comparing against a named competitor or incumbent lifts the launch post.
hypotheses.note: R:P02 is a meta-analysis of comparative advertising, not social posts.

hypotheses.claim: Pitching by analogy to a known product ('Cursor for X') lifts the post.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: A 'first / best / most capable' claim (the first AI software engineer, our most capable model) makes the launch travel.
Opening with stated excitement ('excited to announce') hurts; state the news instead.
hypotheses.note: R:W05 (controlled) says sentiment words help in general; the playbooks say this particular opener is wasted.

hypotheses.claim: Telling the backstory (how long it took, why it was built) lifts the post (build in public).
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: Addressing the reader directly (you / your) in the first line lifts the post.
Pointing at a demonstration (demo, watch, see it in action) lifts the launch post.
A launch video that is framed as a demo does better than another launch video.
Saying the product is available now (labs' availability line) lifts the post.
Announcing something that is not yet available ('coming soon') does worse.
Celebration emoji (rocket, party, fire) lift the post.
Mentioning the Product Hunt / Hacker News launch in the X post helps it.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: For a model release, a video of the model doing something beats no media.
For a model release, an image (typically a benchmark chart) beats no media.
Several images do better than one.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: Within model releases, the open-weights ones travel further.
Model releases are the launches that travel furthest for an AI account.
hypotheses.note: A topic, not something a writer chooses; reported so that the model can condition on it.

hypotheses.claim: Launch on a weekday morning Pacific time (06:00 to 11:59 PT).
hypotheses.note: Vendor timing studies are pooled across accounts, in the poster's local time, and disagree with each other (X:P09, X:P11).

hypotheses.claim: The 8 to 10am Pacific weekday slot is best.
hypotheses.note: PB070 (79 founder tweets) claims 3 to 5 times the median impressions for the Tuesday / Wednesday morning slot.

hypotheses.claim: Tuesday to Thursday morning Pacific is best.
Weekday morning beats weekday afternoon Pacific.
hypotheses.note: Buffer says morning, Sprout says noon to 6pm.

hypotheses.claim: Weekday morning beats evening and night Pacific.
hypotheses.note: Metricool says 9pm is best.

hypotheses.claim: Tuesday is the best launch day.
Weekend launches do worse.
A teaser in the days before ('tomorrow', 'something is coming') lifts the launch post.
A teaser the day before lifts the launch post.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: Do not post in the 24 hours before the launch (an account's posts compete with each other).
hypotheses.note: The code decays an author's 2nd and 3rd post within one feed request; the launch track found the 2-hour version (grade C).

hypotheses.claim: Launch repeatedly / run a launch week: several launch posts within days of each other each do well.
hypotheses.note: The playbook claim is about total reach over the week; what we can test is each post against the account's other launch posts.

hypotheses.claim: Follow up in the days after by quote-posting your own launch (a milestone, '24 hours later').
hypotheses.note: Circular: launches that did well get followed up. See _context_extra for how the follow-up posts themselves do.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: Follow-up announcements in the days after help the launch.
Keep posting in the days after the launch.
Other accounts quote-posting within the first hour lifts the launch (early engagement compounds).
hypotheses.note: The controlled evidence (random early upvotes, donations) is from other platforms. In our corpus the comparison is circular: launches that are taking off get quoted sooner.

hypotheses.claim: Employees and founders quote-posting the company's launch within the first hour lifts the launch.
When the team does quote-post, doing it within the first hour beats doing it later the same day.
hypotheses.note: The least circular version available: both sides were quoted by the team. Still partly circular and thin.
hypotheses.level: every account pooled (too thin among company and founder accounts)

hypotheses.claim: A quote by another account within the first hour beats a first quote that comes later.
A link in the post body costs reach.
hypotheses.note: Launch posts without an external link won 58.2%. The size (1.29x likes) is far below the 4 to 8x views gap of R:K01, and X's product head denies any penalty (X:S03, X:S04); the code has none (X:C15).

hypotheses.claim: Put the link in a reply instead.
hypotheses.note: 17 pairs; replies are not in the corpus.

hypotheses.claim: A launch needs a video.
hypotheses.note: Video against no media 65.4%, against an image 62.8% (grade B; weaker after April 2026).

hypotheses.claim: Text posts beat video posts on X (2025).
hypotheses.note: For launch posts inside the same account, video wins 65.4% against no media. Buffer's result is engagement per impression pooled across accounts; ours is likes against the account's own usual.

hypotheses.claim: Adding an image raises engagement.
hypotheses.note: 59.5% in pairs but likes ratio 1.17x (0.95 to 1.45) and 48.0% among clear launch posts.

hypotheses.claim: Write the launch as a thread.
hypotheses.note: Only the head post's thread marker is visible: 51.2% (45.5 to 56.9). The thread body is not in the corpus.

hypotheses.claim: Hashtags help (1 to 2 hashtags, +21%).
hypotheses.note: 41 launch posts with a hashtag; the version without won 60.2% (43.4 to 76.6). X's code has no hashtag term and X's owner told users to stop (X:S10).

hypotheses.claim: Tagging other accounts lowers sharing.
hypotheses.note: Same direction as Tan, Lee and Pang: no tags won 59.1% (52.9 to 64.4) but the likes ratio 1.18x (0.99 to 1.41) includes no effect.

hypotheses.claim: Open the launch on the pain point, not on the product ('hook first, product second').
hypotheses.note: The playbooks say this about the launch VIDEO. For the post TEXT the opposite holds: opening with the announcement won 72.5% (59.5 to 81.8) over opening with a problem or question, and naming the product in the first line won 64.0% (grade A).

hypotheses.claim: Informative, specific first lines win (proper nouns, numbers).
hypotheses.note: First line names the product: 64.0% (59.0 to 69.0), confirmed before and after April 2026.

hypotheses.claim: Shorter is better (trim 10 to 20%).
hypotheses.note: Length shows no effect either way (280+ characters: adjusted 0.95x); layout on 3+ lines helps (59.2%).

hypotheses.claim: Posts close together from one account suppress each other.
hypotheses.note: Launch within 2 hours of the previous post: 0.71x (0.58 to 0.87) pooled over all accounts (grade C).

hypotheses.claim: Quote-posting your own announcement instead of posting it as an original costs reach.
hypotheses.note: Original against quote: 72.1% (60.7 to 81.1), grade B.

hypotheses.claim: Launch video length of 45 to 90 seconds is best; over 10 seconds is needed for the video-quality-view action.
hypotheses.note: duration_ms is empty for all 852 video launch posts in the corpus. The code's video weights are all zero in any case (X:C09).

hypotheses.claim: Replies from well-known accounts and replying to commenters lift the post.
hypotheses.note: Replies are not in the corpus.

hypotheses.claim: Post the launch from the founder's account, not the company's.
hypotheses.note: Team membership is not observable. What the launch track could measure points the other way: launch posts get 2.2x the usual on company accounts and 2.3x on founder accounts, and a team member's first-person quote got more likes than the company's own post in 10% of 152 cases.

hypotheses.claim: Paid amplification (clippers, creator blocks, ads) is what produces the large view counts.
hypotheses.note: Paid and organic views are not separable in public counts, and views exist for only 205 launch posts here.

hypotheses.claim: Controversy / rage bait is distribution.
hypotheses.note: No reliable label for provocation; negative reactions are not observable (replies, mutes, blocks), and the code weights those at -31 to -234 (X:C02).

hypotheses.claim: Images with a human face lift engagement (38 to 291% on Twitter).
hypotheses.note: Needs image content; left to the media track.

hypotheses.claim: Premium accounts get about 10x reach.
hypotheses.note: Cannot be measured inside an account; outside sources conflict (Buffer 10x pooled; a 2023 feed audit found no boost; no multiplier in the 2026 code).

hypotheses.claim: A curator or well-known account sharing the work is the largest lever for AI work (2 to 3x citations).
hypotheses.note: Reposts are not in the corpus; quote posts by large accounts are circular (see H46).
